Facts as are found from the impugned order are that the accused-petitioner was facing trial in special Tribunal Case No. 12 of 1993 for an offence under section 3 of the Explosive Substance Act before Special Tribunal No. IV, Bagerhat. Evidence and examination of the accused were complete. The case was fixed for argument when the Informant filed an unsworn application before the Sessions Judge, Bagerhat for transfer of the case to any other Tribunal making some allegations against Special Tribunal No. IV. The learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 30.7.96 after hearing the parties transferred the case to Special Tribunal No. II by merely observing that since allegations were made against the judge and the informant came to entertain doubt about the presiding Judge of the Tribunal, the case should be transferred. The accused petitioner then took a revision under sec-tion 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the High Court Division against the said order. It was argued, inter alia, that since the transfer petition was neither supported by affidavit or affirmation as required under section 526 (4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Sessions judge ought not to have acted upon the same. 

 “In a case like this we are inclined to invoke inherent jurisdiction under section 56IA Cr. P.C. and direct that the case should be tried by the special Tribunal presided over by the Sessions judge himself 

 8. Then again it is difficult to see why the High Court Division should have made another transfer to the Special Tribunal (Sessions Judge) when there was no objection to Special Tribunal No. II where transfer was already made. The High Court Division was moved in the revision-al jurisdiction and it had ample power to pass any order for ends of justice there under. Why then was it necessary to invoke section 561A Cr. P.C.? Why an order was passed to register the matter as a Miscellaneous Case when the petition was moved under section 439 Cr. P.C.?
